clue.text: Sign wild pig's been shot, daughter notices here

parts.note: a wild pig is a boar; if it has been shot there is a bullet in the boar, so the phrase is read literally as BULLET IN BOAR
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A hunting notice reporting that a wild boar has been shot, which a daughter spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' acts as a link pointing to the definition: what follows tells you where notices are posted.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinboard in an office or hall is the place where announcements and notices are put up.

clue.text: Making water sport up, then one on land

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a common abbreviation for the sport
I is the Roman numeral one
a land or country is a nation

explanation.surface: A pun on water sports: making water as a sporting activity on dry land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making water' looks like a water sport, but it is a polite expression for peeing.
explanation.definitionFit: Making water is a euphemism for passing urine.

clue.text: Vote to Leave behaving carelessly? They're no experts

indicators.note: to leave means the vote mark must depart from the word for careless behaviour

parts.note: laxity is slackness, the quality of behaving carelessly
X is the cross marked on a ballot paper to cast a vote

explanation.surface: A jibe at the Brexit referendum: voting Leave as careless behaviour by non-experts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vote to Leave' reads as the Brexit referendum, but it tells you to remove X from LAXITY.
explanation.definitionFit: The laity are ordinary people without professional or specialist knowledge, as opposed to clergy or experts.

clue.text: Fed up with banks, head of Exchequer quits

indicators.note: quits means the letter leaves, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: something tiered has banks or rows rising one above another

indicators.note: head of signals the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Frustration with the banks causes the head of the Exchequer to resign.
explanation.walkthrough: TIERED loses its first E (the head of 'Exchequer'), leaving TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being weary or sick of something is a common sense of being fed up.

clue.text: Where top Tory is less sensitive after tax rises

indicators.note: after means the reversed piece comes behind the word for less sensitive

parts.note: number is the comparative of numb, more numb or less sensitive

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: net here is the verb meaning to take or clear as profit, loosely glossed as tax

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister grows callous once taxes go up.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as 'more numb', not as a figure. Number Ten Downing Street is the official home of the British Prime Minister, who is the top Tory when the Conservatives govern.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister's London residence is at 10 Downing Street, where the Conservative leader lives when in office.

clue.text: Likely losers having borderline personalities?

definitions.meaning: competitors not expected to win, rank long shots in a race
people who sit at the border or edge, read whimsically as figures on the outer edge

explanation.surface: Musing on whether underdogs have borderline personality traits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borderline personalities' suggests a psychiatric term, but here it means people literally on the outside edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Long shots in betting are those unlikely to win; also people at the edge of a group are not insiders.

clue.text: Teacher's pet not bottom

indicators.note: not bottom means the final letter, at the bottom of a down entry, is dropped

parts.note: a rabbit is a common household pet

explanation.surface: Suggests the teacher's pet who is not the worst in the class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' looks like a phrase, but 'Teacher' is the definition and 'pet' gives RABBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious instructor; the word means my master or teacher.

clue.text: In Paris, you and Latvian showered, able to use bathroom

parts.note: toi is French for you, the familiar form
a Lett is a person from Latvia
rained means came down in showers

explanation.surface: A French speaker and a Latvian take showers, which makes them fit to use the bathroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has learnt to use a potty or lavatory unaided is said to be past nappies and ready for the loo.

clue.text: Girl moving cautiously after parking's tight

indicators.note: after means the slow-movement word comes behind the parking letter

parts.note: Penny is a girl's name
P is the usual sign and abbreviation for parking
inching means creeping forward a little at a time

explanation.surface: A girl edges her car forward carefully once parked because the space is tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' seems to describe the parking space; it means mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stingy or miserly with money is to be tight, a colloquial word for mean.

clue.text: Essentially solid competitor's award

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core, so the inner letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: a vier is one who vies, so a competitor

explanation.surface: A dependable competitor receives an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'solid' gives OLI. The Olivier awards are Britain's main theatre prizes, named after the actor Laurence Olivier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Laurence Olivier Awards are the annual London prizes for theatre, so an Olivier is such a prize.

clue.text: I'm not sure about diners possibly changing

indicators.note: about means the hesitation sound is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: um is the noise of uncertainty
a table may be a group of diners seated together, as in a table of six

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating over whether diners might change their minds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something liable to alter or variable in form is described by this Latin-derived adjective.

clue.text: Grassy area outside of fairway and green

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassy field

indicators.note: outside of means the outer letters, first and last, of the next word

explanation.surface: A golf course picture: grass, fairway and green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the putting green but is an adjective meaning full of foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: A district full of trees and foliage looks verdant, the sense of green as abundant with plants.

clue.text: One rejected appeal in parliament, an advocate of regime change?

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Diet of Japan
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rejected means the word for appeal is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: it means sex appeal, as in someone who has it

explanation.surface: A politician whose appeal was turned down in parliament wants a change of regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regime change' suggests a coup; here it is a change of eating regime. 'in' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nutrition expert recommends altered eating plans, so is a supporter of a change of regimen, punningly.

clue.text: Experience one drug, another is junk

parts.note: a trip is the experience of taking a hallucinogen
E is ecstasy, another drug

explanation.surface: A druggie's verdict: one drug is an experience, another is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is offal from a cow's stomach, and colloquially worthless nonsense or rubbish.

clue.text: Stripped-off character admits quite bad manners

indicators.note: admits means the shuffled letters are let inside the trimmed word
stripped off means its outer letters are taken away

parts.note: a letter is a written character of the alphabet

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of quite are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A person who strips off and confesses to bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripped-off' trims the character to ETTE and 'bad' shuffles the next word into IQUET, which 'admits' places inside. 'Stripped-off character' suggests a nudist, not a trimmed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour, the accepted manners of society.

clue.text: Flower flatter round front of calyx

indicators.note: round means the flattery phrase goes around the letter

parts.note: to butter up is to flatter

indicators.note: front of signals the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Praising the calyx at the front of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower flatter' suggests something botanical; 'flatter' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a yellow meadow bloom of the ranunculus family.

clue.text: Concerned with bloomers, say, ban coital frolics

indicators.note: frolics suggests romping about, so the letters are played around into a new order

explanation.surface: A racy picture of underwear and a ban on lovemaking frolics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests knickers; it means things that bloom, plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relating to the study of plants and flowers, which bloom, is concerned with plants.

clue.text: Cleaner French ruler somewhere in Belgium

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a cleaner in British English
le roi is French for the king

explanation.surface: A cleaner and a French king somewhere in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Charleroi is an industrial city in the Hainaut province of Belgium.

clue.text: Film star right with popular comic character

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Tintin is the boy reporter in Hergé's comic books

explanation.surface: A film star allied with a well-loved cartoon hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Rin Tin Tin was a German shepherd dog who starred in Hollywood films of the 1920s.

clue.text: Small man defending king for sire

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
in chess a pawn is a man often used to shield the king

explanation.surface: A little man protecting the king on behalf of His Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sire' looks like a form of address to a king; it is the verb meaning to father.
explanation.definitionFit: To father offspring and to produce young are both senses of the verb, used of animals.

clue.text: Reason to be in bed with nun, if zeal lapses

indicators.note: lapses suggests falling away from proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scandalous scenario of bedding a nun whose religious zeal slips.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a seduction; the bed is a sickbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Flu is an illness that commonly confines a sufferer to bed.

clue.text: Scottish runner said to be just out of the medals

indicators.note: said signals that the word sounds like the one entered

parts.note: in a race, finishing fourth means narrowly missing the medal places

explanation.surface: A Scottish athlete who finished just outside the medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forth is a major river in Scotland, and rivers are runners in crossword parlance because they run.

clue.text: Something acquired a second time

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a gain is something acquired

explanation.surface: Something got once and then again.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split into A GAIN gives the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Once more or anew means a repeated occurrence, a second time.

clue.text: Release of gas bomb El Chapo carries

indicators.note: carries means the phrase holds the letters within it

explanation.surface: A drug lord transporting a gas bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: El Chapo is the Mexican drug lord Joaquín Guzmán.
explanation.definitionFit: A burp lets wind out of the stomach through the mouth.

clue.text: Where Long Beach is? West, as a rule

parts.note: Long Beach, California, lies near Los Angeles, so it is by LA

explanation.surface: A question of geography: Long Beach is out west, as a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A bylaw is a regulation made by a local authority, a rule for a locality.

clue.text: Not even Cartier is at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or lost, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The jewellery firm Cartier is out of its depth and uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular and unpredictable, the opposite of steady or even.

clue.text: Trouble rook, one flying round? It's on the wing

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the chess letter
flying means the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A bird-watching scene: a troubled rook flying round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' turns ONE into EON, which goes round R to make ERON. 'wing' suggests a bird; it is an aircraft wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is the hinged flap on an aircraft's wing used to control roll.

clue.text: Hit moves keeping dance modern and trendy, a must for parties

indicators.note: keeping means the shuffled letters hold the dance inside them
moves signals the letters of the word move about

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
new means modern
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: A dance-floor hit that is modern and trendy is essential at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' suggests celebrations; they are political parties. A three-line whip is a strict Westminster instruction to MPs to vote with their party.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics a whip underlined three times orders members to attend and vote as instructed, a compulsory obligation.
